name: Bengali akshara word-puzzle vocabulary
audience: children ~7 years old learning to read
HOW_TO_READ_THIS: An AKSHARA is one game tile: a consonant cluster plus its vowel sign, or an independent vowel.
মাছ = মা + ছ (2 tiles). কলম = ক + ল + ম (3 tiles). কমলা = ক + ম + লা (3 tiles).
A bare consonant carrying no vowel sign is its own tile. A conjunct is ONE tile (কচ্ছপ = ক + চ্ছ + প).
Each level's 'wheel' is the set of DISTINCT aksharas across its words. It is never more than 7.
Every word in the level is buildable from the wheel tiles, and tiles may be reused within a word.
type=akshara: every word starts with the SAME akshara (level 'key'). These teach the কার/মাত্রা series.
type=letter: every word starts with the same LETTER but different matras. Used where a single akshara could not fill a wheel.
RULES_THE_WORDS_ALREADY_SATISFY: Concrete: a picture can replace the gloss. Or a number, a colour, or an everyday action.
Dictionary base forms. No verb inflections, case endings or plurals.
Bangladeshi Bengali. No West Bengal-only words (no জল/কাকা/পিসি/দিদি/লঙ্কা - use পানি/চাচা/ফুফু/আপা/মরিচ).
No two spellings of the same word. Each word appears in exactly one level.
CRITICAL_ENCODING_WARNING: ড় ঢ় য় are Unicode COMPOSITION EXCLUSIONS. NFC will NOT unify the precomposed letters
Both forms occur in real Bengali text. If you compare a player's tile taps against a stored
word without canonicalising, roughly 12% of ordinary words silently fail to match -
including ঘোড়া, ঘড়ি, মেয়ে, পড়া, চেয়ার. Normalise BOTH sides to the precomposed form first.
The 'split' array in this file is already correctly segmented - use it, do not re-derive it.

FIELD_NOTES.split: its aksharas, in order - one tile each
FIELD_NOTES.en: one or two word English gloss, intended as the illustration brief
FIELD_NOTES.freq: frequency in a Bengali spoken corpus (film subtitles). 0 is common and NOT a defect: the corpus underrepresents household nouns like ডাব, দই, শালিক.
FIELD_NOTES.flag: present only when the word needs care. regional-BD = Bangladesh-specific. Others are illustration or familiarity caveats.
